passages.text: “As for you, take up a lament for the princes of Israel and say: ‘What was your mother? A lioness among the lions! She lay down among the young lions; she reared her cubs.
passages.sermon:
God spoke to the prophet Ezekiel.
God told Ezekiel to speak to the princes of Israel.
God told Ezekiel to sing a lament for them.
God told Ezekiel to ask about their mother.
Their mother was like a lioness.
She lived among other lions.
She lay down among young lions.
She raised her cubs among them.
passages.original: וְאַתָּה֙ שָׂ֣א קִינָ֔ה אֶל־ נְשִׂיאֵ֖י יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃ וְאָמַרְתָּ֗ מָ֤ה אִמְּךָ֙ לְבִיָּ֔א בֵּ֥ין אֲרָי֖וֹת רָבָ֑צָה בְּת֥וֹךְ כְּפִרִ֖ים רִבְּתָ֥ה גוּרֶֽיהָ׃

passages.text: She brought up one of her cubs, and he became a young lion. After learning to tear his prey, he devoured men.
passages.sermon:
A lioness raised one of her cubs.
This cub grew into a young lion.
He learned to hunt and catch prey.
He killed and ate people.
passages.original: וַתַּ֛עַל אֶחָ֥ד מִגֻּרֶ֖יהָ כְּפִ֣יר הָיָ֑ה וַיִּלְמַ֥ד לִטְרָף־ טֶ֖רֶף אָדָ֥ם אָכָֽל׃

passages.text: When the nations heard of him, he was trapped in their pit. With hooks they led him away to the land of Egypt.
passages.sermon:
The nations heard about the young lion.
The nations set a trap for him.
The young lion was caught in their pit.
The nations put hooks in him.
They led him away to Egypt.
passages.original: וַיִּשְׁמְע֥וּ אֵלָ֛יו גּוֹיִ֖ם בְּשַׁחְתָּ֣ם נִתְפָּ֑שׂ וַיְבִאֻ֥הוּ בַֽחַחִ֖ים אֶל־ אֶ֥רֶץ מִצְרָֽיִם׃

passages.text: When she saw that she had waited in vain, that her hope was lost, she took another of her cubs and made him a young lion.
passages.sermon:
A mother lion waited for something good to happen.
She saw that nothing good came.
She realized her hope was gone.
She had cubs.
She took another one of her cubs.
She made this cub into a young lion.
passages.original: וַתֵּ֙רֶא֙ כִּ֣י נֽוֹחֲלָ֔ה אָבְדָ֖ה תִּקְוָתָ֑הּ וַתִּקַּ֛ח אֶחָ֥ד מִגֻּרֶ֖יהָ כְּפִ֥יר שָׂמָֽתְהוּ׃

passages.text: He prowled among the lions, and became a young lion. After learning to tear his prey, he devoured men.
passages.sermon:
He was a young lion.
He walked among other lions.
He learned to hunt prey.
He ate people.
passages.original: וַיִּתְהַלֵּ֥ךְ בְּתוֹךְ־ אֲרָי֖וֹת כְּפִ֣יר הָיָ֑ה וַיִּלְמַ֥ד לִטְרָף־ טֶ֖רֶף אָדָ֥ם אָכָֽל׃

passages.text: He broke down their strongholds and devastated their cities. The land and everything in it shuddered at the sound of his roaring.
passages.sermon:
The young lion attacked people.
He made many women widows.
He destroyed their cities.
He ruined their strongholds.
His roaring frightened the whole land.
Everything in the land trembled at his roar.
passages.original: וַיֵּ֙דַע֙ אַלְמְנוֹתָ֔יו וְעָרֵיהֶ֖ם הֶחֱרִ֑יב וַתֵּ֤שַׁם אֶ֙רֶץ֙ וּמְלֹאָ֔הּ מִקּ֖וֹל שַׁאֲגָתֽוֹ׃

passages.text: Then the nations set out against him from the provinces on every side. They spread their net over him; he was trapped in their pit.
passages.sermon:
Many nations surrounded him.
These nations came from every province.
They set out against him.
They spread their net over him.
They trapped him in their pit.
passages.original: וַיִּתְּנ֨וּ עָלָ֥יו גּוֹיִ֛ם סָבִ֖יב מִמְּדִינ֑וֹת וַֽיִּפְרְשׂ֥וּ עָלָ֛יו רִשְׁתָּ֖ם בְּשַׁחְתָּ֥ם נִתְפָּֽשׂ׃

passages.text: With hooks they caged him and brought him to the king of Babylon. They brought him into captivity so that his roar was heard no longer on the mountains of Israel.
passages.sermon:
The nations attacked the ruler of Israel.
They trapped him with hooks.
They put him in a cage.
They took him to the king of Babylon.
They led him away as a captive.
He could not roar anymore.
No one heard his voice again on the mountains of Israel.
passages.original: וַֽיִּתְּנֻ֤הוּ בַסּוּגַר֙ בַּֽחַחִ֔ים וַיְבִאֻ֖הוּ אֶל־ מֶ֣לֶךְ בָּבֶ֑ל יְבִאֻ֙הוּ֙ בַּמְּצֹד֔וֹת לְמַ֗עַן לֹא־ יִשָּׁמַ֥ע קוֹל֛וֹ ע֖וֹד אֶל־ הָרֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃פ

passages.text: Your mother was like a vine in your vineyard, planted by the water; it was fruitful and full of branches because of the abundant waters.
passages.sermon:
Your mother was like a vine.
She grew in your vineyard.
She was planted by the water.
She was fruitful.
She had many branches.
She grew well because there was much water.
passages.original: אִמְּךָ֥ כַגֶּ֛פֶן בְּדָמְךָ֖ עַל־ מַ֣יִם שְׁתוּלָ֑ה פֹּֽרִיָּה֙ וַֽעֲנֵפָ֔ה הָיְתָ֖ה מִמַּ֥יִם רַבִּֽים׃

passages.text: It had strong branches, fit for a ruler’s scepter. It towered high above the thick branches, conspicuous for its height and for its dense foliage.
passages.sermon:
The vine had strong branches.
These branches were fit for a ruler’s scepter.
The vine grew very tall.
It stood above the thick branches around it.
People could see its great height.
People could see its many leaves.
passages.original: וַיִּֽהְיוּ־ לָ֞הּ מַטּ֣וֹת עֹ֗ז אֶל־ שִׁבְטֵי֙ מֹֽשְׁלִ֔ים וַתִּגְבַּ֥הּ קֽוֹמָת֖וֹ עַל־ בֵּ֣ין עֲבֹתִ֑ים וַיֵּרָ֣א בְגָבְה֔וֹ בְּרֹ֖ב דָּלִיֹּתָֽיו׃

passages.text: But it was uprooted in fury, cast down to the ground, and the east wind dried up its fruit. Its strong branches were stripped off and they withered; the fire consumed them.
passages.sermon:
The mother is like a vine.
God became angry with the vine.
God uprooted the vine in fury.
God threw the vine down to the ground.
The east wind blew on the vine.
The east wind dried up the vine’s fruit.
The vine’s strong branches broke off.
The strong branches withered.
Fire burned the strong branches.
Fire destroyed them.
passages.original: וַתֻּתַּ֤שׁ בְּחֵמָה֙ לָאָ֣רֶץ הֻשְׁלָ֔כָה וְר֥וּחַ הַקָּדִ֖ים הוֹבִ֣ישׁ פִּרְיָ֑הּ הִתְפָּרְק֧וּ וְיָבֵ֛שׁוּ מַטֵּ֥ה עֻזָּ֖הּ אֵ֥שׁ אֲכָלָֽתְהוּ׃

passages.text: Now it is planted in the wilderness, in a dry and thirsty land.
passages.sermon:
The subject is a vine.
The vine was once strong and fruitful.
Now the vine is planted in the wilderness.
The wilderness is a dry land.
The wilderness is a thirsty land.
passages.original: וְעַתָּ֖ה שְׁתוּלָ֣ה בַמִּדְבָּ֑ר בְּאֶ֖רֶץ צִיָּ֥ה וְצָמָֽא׃

passages.text: Fire has gone out from its main branch and devoured its fruit; on it no strong branch remains fit for a ruler’s scepter.’ This is a lament and shall be used as a lament.”
passages.sermon:
God spoke to Ezekiel.
God described Israel as a vine.
Fire came out from the vine’s main branch.
The fire destroyed the vine’s fruit.
No strong branch remained on the vine.
No branch was left that could become a ruler’s scepter.
This is a lament.
People must use it as a lament.
passages.original: וַתֵּצֵ֨א אֵ֜שׁ מִמַּטֵּ֤ה בַדֶּ֙יהָ֙ פִּרְיָ֣הּ אָכָ֔לָה וְלֹא־ הָ֥יָה בָ֛הּ מַטֵּה־ עֹ֖ז שֵׁ֣בֶט לִמְשׁ֑וֹל קִ֥ינָה הִ֖יא וַתְּהִ֥י לְקִינָֽה׃פ
